signals.title: Buell’s 400bhp Project Leviathan made its Bonneville debut, but its best run fell well short of the 250mph target.
signals.summary: Buell’s 400bhp Project Leviathan has completed its first Bonneville Speed Week, recording a best speed of 178.531mph after a challenging debut on the salt. Remember that 400bhp Buell that was heading to Bonneville with a 250mph target? Well, we now know how that went, and things didn’t exactly go to plan. Project Leviathan previously set its sights on breaking the 250mph barrier, although the bike's best recorded run, that we can find, was 178.531mph. That is obviously some way short of the headline target, but the circumstances around Leviathan’s first attempt at Bonneville aren't clear-cut, with outside influences helping to stifle the team. For starters, neither the bike nor its rider, Jacob Stark, had ever competed at Bonneville before. The Speed Week outing was the first time Leviathan had moved under its own power outside of testing and dyno work, while Stark had never ridden on the salt. Before the team could even start chasing big numbers, they had to work through the Bonneville licensing process, which requires riders to demonstrate that they can control their machines at increasing speeds. The first run was deliberately straightforward, as Stark needed to maintain more than 125mph to secure a ‘D’ licence, and the team kept things simple with a short-shift into second gear before returning to the pits for inspection and adjustment. signals.title: The IGA is pushing for a BIG jump in the cost of an MOT
signals.summary: Independent Garage Association says current MOT fee is no longer sustainable, with motorcycle tests also caught up in the proposed increase Motorcycle MOT prices could be heading upwards after the Independent Garage Association (IGA) called for the Government to significantly increase the maximum MOT fee. The IGA says the current MOT fee has become unsustainable for independent garages, with inflation only one part of a wider rise in operating costs. It wants the maximum fee for an MOT to increase to at least £95, although it has yet to confirm what this would mean specifically for motorcycle MOTs. Importantly for bikers, the IGA has confirmed to Visordown that its case for an increase does include motorcycle MOTs. The current maximum fee for a motorcycle MOT is £29.65, meaning any substantial increase could have a noticeable impact on the cost of keeping a bike legally on the road. However, the IGA has not yet confirmed whether it is proposing that motorcycle MOTs should rise to £95, or what figure it will put forward when it enters discussions with the Government. Visordown has asked the IGA for clarification on what it believes the new motorcycle MOT fee should be, but no figure had been provided at the time of publication. signals.title: London ride out in support of Iran prisoners Lindsay and Craig Foreman announced
signals.summary: Bikers are set to show their support for British couple Lindsay and Craig Foreman, who have now been held in an Iranian prison for over 600 days. A special ride out is set to take place in London on September 9, as part of a campaign to try and bring justice for British couple Lindsay and Craig Foreman, who remain detained in Iran. It has now been 600 days since the motorcycle couple were placed in jail, with both sentenced to a decade in prison after being convicted of espionage charges in February 2026. Craig Foreman has since been handed an additional two years in jail on top of his 10-year sentence. This was confirmed to Craig Foreman by a judge when the motorcyclist believed he was meeting with his lawyer. The extra two-year sentence was for speaking to media outlets while incarcerated. The couple were originally arrested when travelling through Iran during an overland motorcycle journey towards Australia, and they have maintained their innocence ever since. The ride out in London will be the second of its kind, after bikers first united when the couple hit 500 days in jail. On that occasion a gathering of adventure bikers rode into Parliament Square on May 20. Next month’s ride out will see riders meet at Queen’s Gate, with bikers urged to arrive at 9:30am before departing at around 10am. It will then end at Parliament Square, where the Prime Minister and MP’s will gather for Prime Minister's Questions (PMQ). Taking part in the ride out is free, and can be booked on the

signals.title: The intriguing details behind Kawasaki’s Hydrogen-powered horse
signals.summary: A new patent has revealed further details of Kawasaki’s Corleo concept, including what the rider must wear to make the thing move. Kawasaki likes to make a splash every now and then, but not even the bonkers H2 could match the collective gasp made when its Corleo concept was launched. Looking more like an equine/feline crossbreed than a motorcycle, the machine was first revealed as a concept in April 2025, with Kawasaki confirming that production development was underway in December the same year. Now, though, we get our first actual details of how the machine will work and how the rider will interact with it. Obviously, a machine with four legs and a head is going to need a different control method, which is exactly what Kawasaki has done. First off, to actually ride the thing, you’ll need a special piece of clothing, decked out with the kind of IMUs you normally find on the inside of a motorcycle. The suit measures and tracks the rider’s movements, even calculating their centre of gravity to steer and control the bike. That’s out-of-the-box thinking at its finest, but when you think about it, it makes a lot of sense. Horse riders and bikers have one thing in common: we use our bodies to help steer our steeds. It seems as though Kawasaki is taking a leaf out of the horse riding playbook to make its four-legged adventure vehicle controllable. signals.title: Group of Royal Enfield Himalayan 750s spotted in unusual place
signals.summary: A group of Royal Enfield Himalayan 750 development bikes appear to have run their course after being spotted at a scrapyard. As the launch of Royal Enfield’s all-new Himalayan 750 draws closer, a group of test mules appear to have reached the end of their development phase after being spotted at a very unusual location. Images on social media show a line of six Himalayan 750 bikes lying on the ground at a scrapyard. Although these bikes were development models only, seeing them deserted at a scrapyard like this is a sad reality of what some bikes go through at the end of their life cycle. It's believed that these bikes were left near the company's R&D centre in the UK. This would make quite a lot of sense, as Royal Enfield operates its UK Technology Centre from Bruntingthorpe, Leicestershire, which plays a crucial role in the development of the company’s global products. The new Himalayan 750 is currently being developed by members of Royal Enfield’s engineering teams in both India and the UK, while the new model was recently spotted testing in the UK, making it likely that these bikes could have been part of those tests. In some ways, these photos do offer a positive narrative, which is that the arrival of the production-ready Himalayan 750 is edging closer. However, seeing images like these does beg the question of whether there’s a better solution for what happens to bikes used for development purposes only. signals.title: Would you subscribe to your next motorcycle? Honda thinks you might
signals.summary: Could subscribing to an electric motorcycle reduce the risk of depreciation? And could subscription ownership eventually replace buying bikes? Honda is taking a different approach to selling its WN7 electric motorcycle in Australia, but could subscription ownership actually make more sense for electric bikes? And is this the future of motorcycles generally? You may also like to read our Honda WN7 review . Buying a new motorcycle has traditionally been a fairly simple transaction. You hand over some money, the bike becomes yours, and somewhere down the line you either sell it, trade it in or keep it until the wheels fall off. What happens to its value in between is your problem. That last bit could become increasingly important as electric motorcycles become more common. Honda's WN7 is an interesting example. The firm's first full-size production electric motorcycle costs £12,999 in the UK, puts out up to 67bhp and has a claimed range of 87 miles under WMTC testing. It’s also, by motorcycle standards, an expensive machine. A CB1000 Hornet SP costs considerably less, goes much faster and a fair bit further between fill-ups. The biggest difference, though, is how it’s powered, and that raises some obvious questions about how much the bike will be worth a few years down the line. The fact of the matter is that most electric bikes are fairly expensive to buy and tend not to hold their value terribly well. For many would-be electric bike riders, that is a big problem. signals.title: Maria Costello reveals “nerve wracking” feeling after race track return
signals.summary: Maria Costello has made her first appearance at a race track since suffering life-changing injuries at the 2026 Isle of Man TT. Maria Costello has made her return to the motorcycle racing scene by attending the Thruxton BSB round this weekend, making it her first appearance at a race track since suffering life-changing injuries at the 2026 Isle of Man TT. Costello was hospitalised alongside sidecar passenger Shaun Parker, with both competitors revealing several updates regarding their condition on social media, since the accident. For Costello, the accident left the female racer paralysed, while she also suffered several other injuries including a broken arm, multiple broken ribs, a broken sternum, a broken nose and eye socket, as well as a Grade 4 liver laceration and facial injuries. These injuries have led to a recovery process that Costello described as “the biggest challenge of my life” in June. However, she has now made her first public appearance at a race track, after attending Saturday’s action at the Thruxton BSB round. Costello shared images of her return on social media, while also hinting at another update on her condition in the near future. The former Isle of Man TT podium finisher said: “Who knew that visiting a motorcycle race could be as nerve wracking and emotionally charged and yet so filled with bliss as yesterday? signals.title: Insta360 drops all-new 8k camera, and this is what it means for motorcyclists
signals.summary: Insta360 has just revealed its new flagship X6 camera which offers a dedicated motorcycle set, upgraded windproof 360 microphones, and a new 2600mAh Xtreme Battery that records 140 minutes of 8K30fps 360 video footage on a single charge. Insta360’s all-new X6 camera could take your content-creating experience on two wheels to the next level. The company’s new flagship camera arrives with plenty of updates, one of which is focused on how much light gets let through to the sensors, which is claimed to be more than any other X model ever. The new X6 makes use of custom dual Sony 1/1.1-inch square sensors that deliver full 360 imaging, as well as 33 per cent more sensor area than the X5, and around four times the light intake per frame, according to Insta360. However, the headline feature of the new X6 is its three-in-one camera system, allowing it to be used as a 360 camera, a subject-tracking flat camera, and a single-lens action cam. Where it gets interesting for motorcyclists is the new 2600mAh Xtreme Battery, which claims to be able to record 140 minutes of 8K30fps 360 video on a single charge. To give you an idea, that is 51 per cent longer than the X5. The new X6 can also fast charge from empty to 80 per cent in just 24 minutes, meaning if you run out of juice while riding, you won’t have to wait long before getting back on the road, provided you have the necessary charging equipment with you. signals.summary: Triumph has revealed a new off-road-based event that is open to all owners of its TF 250 and 450 motocross and enduro motorcycles, as well as four non-Triumph owners. Triumph has launched a new ‘Ride With Legends’ off-road event, making it possible for current owners of its off-road motorcycle range to ride alongside Ricky Carmichael and Ivan Cervantes. The event will take place at Moto101 on Thursday, September 3, which is located at Gonerby Moor, in Lincolnshire. It is open to all owners of a TF 250-X, TF 450-X, TF 250-E and TF 450-E, but this does not include the TF 450-RC Edition. However, there will also be four spots reserved for non-Triumph owners, which are available as part of a prize draw. Entering the competition is very simple and free of charge. All you need to do is fill out the competition form provided by Triumph, which can be found here . This will automatically put you in the draw, which closes on August 23. Those who win a place at the event will also be allowed to bring up to five people to spectate. For current Triumph TF 250 and 450 owners, pre-event registration can be done via the company’s owners registration form. Attendance is also free of charge for current Triumph owners. The event will be held at Moto101’s motocross track, where Carmichael will be one of the headline names set to ride the course. signals.title: The Indian Chief Vintage Sturgis, SD Edition is pure two-wheeled Americana
signals.summary: Just 125 examples of the heritage-inspired Indian Chief Vintage Sturgis, SD Edition will be built to mark the firm's 125th anniversary. Indian Motorcycle has pulled the covers off a new limited edition Chief Vintage that celebrates the company's place at the very beginning of the Sturgis Motorcycle Rally. Revealed at the 2026 Sturgis Motorcycle Rally, the Chief Vintage Sturgis, SD Edition arrives at the time of Indian's 125th anniversary, with production for the model also capped at just 125 individually numbered units. While the vast majority will stay in North America, a small allocation is also heading to the UK and a handful of other international markets. The bike is more than just another paint-and-badge special. Indian says it pays tribute to the original gathering in Sturgis back in 1938, when a local Indian Motorcycle dealer and a group of Indian riders organised what would eventually become the world's biggest motorcycle rally. To reflect that history, the bike gets a period-inspired Indian Motorcycle Red and Cream paint scheme along with a multi-coloured Indian headdress logo similar to those used on the firm's bikes during the 1930s. A painted number 56 on the side panel is designed to resemble the hand-painted race numbers worn by competitors at the early Sturgis events, while each bike also carries its own numbered plaque. signals.title: Honda Forza 750, two new colour options are available
signals.summary: Using the same strategy adopted for the 2027 X-ADV 750 and NC750X, Honda has refreshed the Forza 750 with nothing more than an updated colour range. Specifically, the flagship model of the Forza family gains two new colour options. Alongside the returning Mat Warm Ash Metallic, customers can now choose the new Gunmetal Black Metallic , featuring an all-black look, and the elegant Mat Iridium Gray Metallic . From a technical point of view, the Forza 750 remains unchanged since the introduction of the 2025 model year. It can be identified by its headlight with integrated LED daytime running lights and turn indicators. Behind the electrically adjustable windscreen sits a 5-inch full-colour TFT display with Honda RoadSync connectivity. Standard equipment includes cruise control, three-level traction control and five riding modes to manage the 58.6 hp produced by the engine, paired with Honda's Dual Clutch Transmission (DCT). The new Forza 750 is also available in a restricted version for A2 licence holders. The chassis package continues to feature a tubular steel frame, an upside-down front fork, a Pro-Link rear suspension with aluminium swingarm, 17-inch front and 15-inch rear wheels, and radially mounted brake calipers. signals.title: Kappa expands its rider lineup with two smart accessories
signals.summary: With the KPM1 and KBH50 , Kappa is enriching its lineup of universal gear for motorcycles and scooters, offering two practical solutions engineered for both daily commuting and long-haul adventures. The first novelty, the KPM1 , lets riders securely mount their smartphone to handlebars ranging from 22 to 32 mm in diameter, ensuring rock-solid stability on the move. Compact and light, this new smartphone mount features a reinforced nylon chassis with TPU side inserts designed to absorb vibrations and impacts. A quick-detach mechanism makes mounting or removing the phone a breeze, while the adjustable cradle accommodates devices from 65 to 90 mm wide. The second highlight from Kappa is the KBH50 bottle holder . Crafted from a blend of reinforced nylon, silicone, and steel, its design guarantees a firm grip on any tubular bar, fitting motorcycles, scooters, and e-bikes alike. It can securely cradle bottles and flasks with diameters between 32 and 77 mm, and the non-slip silicone interior lining keeps everything locked in place even when tackling bumpy terrain. Praktik ini terjadi ketika sebuah lot parkir kosong "ditandai" dengan cara ada seseorang yang berdiri di titik tersebut, sementara mobil yang bersangkutan belum tiba di lokasi. Kejadian seperti ini kerap memicu gesekan dengan pengemudi lain yang juga hendak mengisi lot yang sama. Kondisi tag parkir, pada akhirnya membutuhkan aturan tertulis yang disepakati bersama, dalam hal ini idealnya berupa aturan internal dari pengelola parkir atau pengelola lokasi setempat. "Makanya butuh sebuah aturan tertulis yang disepakati," kata Rio kepada Kompas.com, Senin (17/8/2026). signals.summary: Molinas dan Risiko Mengulang Proyek Kendaraan Nasional JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com Program Motor Listrik Nasional (Molinas) dinilai memiliki peluang menjadi tonggak industrialisasi kendaraan listrik di Indonesia. Namun, pemerintah perlu memastikan program tersebut tidak berhenti sebatas proyek kendaraan nasional , yang mengandalkan kemampuan perakitan dan dukungan kebijakan. Pengamat otomotif Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB) Yannes Martinus Pasaribu mengatakan, tantangan terbesar Molinas justru berada pada pembangunan industri dan penguasaan teknologi di balik kendaraan listrik. signals.summary: Mobil Hybrid Terlaris Juli 2026; Zenix Pucuk, Tiggo Cross 10 Besar JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com Penjualan mobil hybrid di Indonesia terus menunjukkan geliat pada Juli 2026. Data Gabungan Industri Kendaraan Bermotor Indonesia (Gaikindo), distribusi dari pabrik ke diler ( wholesales ) kendaraan ini mencapai 8.004 unit. Angka tersebut membuat mobil hybrid menyumbang 33,4 persen dari total penjualan kendaraan elektrifikasi atau xEV yang mencapai 23.949 unit sepanjang Juli 2026. Toyota masih mendominasi pasar hybrid. Namun, persaingan di papan atas mulai diwarnai pendatang baru, salah satunya Mitsubishi Xforce HEV yang langsung menempati posisi ketujuh. signals.title: MotoGP 2026, Penantang Juara Dunia Bakal Terlihat di Seri Aragon
signals.summary: MotoGP 2026, Penantang Juara Dunia Bakal Terlihat di Seri Aragon JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - Persaingan perebutan gelar juara dunia MotoGP 2026 memasuki fase krusial. Dengan menyisakan 10 seri balapan dan 370 poin maksimal yang diperebutkan, selisih poin di posisi enam besar klasemen sementara terbilang sangat ketat, yakni hanya berjarak 56 poin. CEO Aprilia Racing, Massimo Rivola , menilai balapan mendatang di Sirkuit MotorLand Aragon, Spanyol, akan menjadi ujian sesungguhnya sekaligus petunjuk kuat siapa penantang sejati gelar juara dunia musim ini. Saat ini, tiga posisi teratas klasemen ditempati oleh para pebalap pengguna Aprilia RS-GP, yaitu Jorge Martin, Marco Bezzecchi, dan Ai Ogura. Menempel ketat di bawahnya ada dua pebalap Ducati, Marc Marquez dan Fabio Di Giannantonio, serta pebalap Trackhouse Aprilia, Raul Fernandez, di urutan keenam.
